findings.what: The verified DuckDB connection is still opened through a mutable pathname rather than the verified file object.
findings.why: The manifest and projection hash are read with O_NOFOLLOW through search_descriptor, but line 214 converts that descriptor back to a pathname and line 215 asks DuckDB to reopen it. A process able to mutate a shared case can rename or ABA-swap .anomaly/search or signals.duckdb after _descriptor_path returns, make DuckDB open a different database, and restore the descriptor-owned artifact before the post-open hash read. That postcheck hashes the name under search_descriptor, not the inode held by the DuckDB connection, so it can pass while search returns attacker-controlled payload rows under the previously verified manifest identity. No shared/exclusive lock or connection-to-file identity check closes this interval; the earlier normal os.replace rebuild race is improved by keeping one connection, but the prior CWE-367/CWE-59 obligation is not fully resolved.

findings.what: Projection staging reintroduces a path-escape write after pinning the private directory.
findings.why: The builder creates and pins a random stage directory, then converts its descriptor to stage_root and passes stage_root/signals.duckdb to DuckDB by pathname. In an existing shared case whose derived directories can be renamed, a local mutator can observe the random entry, rename it, and place a symlink at the pathname before DuckDB opens it. DuckDB does not receive O_NOFOLLOW or a dir_fd, so it can create or modify an out-of-root signals.duckdb before the later descriptor-based read notices that the pinned stage lacks the file. Random naming narrows prediction but does not prevent an observable swap, and the module contains no flock/lockf or equivalent lock. This leaves the prior canonical-containment blocker reachable and can cause out-of-root data corruption even though the build ultimately raises.

evidence.output: Canonical inputs are allowlisted, opened component-by-component with O_NOFOLLOW and dir_fd, read from pinned descriptors, identity-rechecked, and hash-bound. Derived artifact byte reads also use O_NOFOLLOW. However, _descriptor_path is used before both DuckDB write and read opens, and grep found no flock, LOCK_EX/LOCK_SH, lockf, portalocker, filelock, or in-process lock. Lines 119-121 and 214-215 establish the two exploitable check/use intervals recorded above.

The canonical producer hashes sanitized snapshot JSON with SHA-256, names new snapshots with that digest, creates them O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW at mode 0600, records path plus hash in schema-v2 provenance, and strict replay requires the exact detector/hash-derived path and verifies canonical JSON hash plus implementation identity. Projection legacy-name acceptance remains hash-bound and cannot silently substitute bytes, while new canonical runs are content-addressed.

Projection constructs results from an explicit public signal/metadata allowlist, recursively removes sensitive-key fields, redacts credential-shaped text, and never projects private_context. Tests assert exact returned redacted payloads, unchanged canonical digests, stale input rejection/rebuild, content-addressed producer snapshots, concurrent rebuild behavior, and pre/post-validation symlink cases. The tests do not cover a swap after a pinned descriptor is converted back to the pathname DuckDB opens.
